terminal.description: A shell in your workspace where the demo prints three invoices from the billing log.

tasks.title: Catch the invoice that does not add up
tasks.description:
Before you change `invoice.js`, prove the bug with a test. In `src/invoice.test.js`, write tests in the `describe('the ticket')` block that fail on the shop's `invoice()` today and will pass once it is right.

One invoice is not enough. The check runs the tests in that block three times:

- beside the shop's `invoice.js`: they must fail
- beside a right fix: they must pass
- beside a version that mends only the ticket's own invoice: they must fail

It does that on three computers set to different time zones and languages, and a test with no `expect` in it fails.
nextSteps: Run `node src/demo.js` and add up the lines of each invoice yourself.
Import `invoice` and the invoices, and expect the right total for WH-2291.
Add a second invoice that does not add up today, and expect what its lines say.
Run `npx vitest run src/invoice.test.js` and see your tests fail on the shop's code.
hints: The demo prints three invoices. On two of them the invoice line is a penny away from what its lines add up to.
A test does not need to know the right total by heart: it can add up the lines the invoice shows and expect the total to equal that sum.
For WH-2291 the lines' VAT is 11.90 and 5.06, so the invoice VAT should be their sum, and the total the net plus that VAT. Do the same for WH-2297.

tasks.title: Make every invoice add up
tasks.description:
Fix `invoice(lines, vatPercent)` in `src/invoice.js` so every invoice is right to the penny. Keep the shape it returns: `{ lines: [{ title, net, vat }], net, vat, total }`, every amount as text with two decimals.

- A line's net is `fee * copies`. Fees have at most two decimals.
- A line's VAT is `vatPercent` of its net, rounded to the nearest penny on that line, with exactly half a penny going up. A rate may have one decimal, such as 17.5.
- The invoice's net, VAT and total are the sums of what the lines show.
- An invoice with no lines is `'0.00'` everywhere.

The check compares your invoices with the right ones for a few cases and a few hundred more, on five computers.
nextSteps: Turn each fee into whole pence once, before you multiply.
Work out each line's VAT in pence, from a rate with no decimals left, and round it there, once.
Add up the lines in pence and turn pence into text only at the very end.
Run your tests and `node src/demo.js` again.
hints: The cause is not `toFixed` itself. Amounts like 1.86 and 1.075 cannot be stored exactly as decimal numbers, so every step works on a value that is a hair off, and the totals are rounded apart from their lines.
Whole numbers are exact. `Math.round(fee * 100)` turns a fee with two decimals into pence, and sums and products of pence never drift.
Keep a line's net and VAT in pence, turn the rate into whole tenths of a percent, round the VAT once with `Math.round`, add the lines up in pence, and divide by 100 only when you format the text.

tasks.title: Write the test for the case next door
tasks.description:
The ticket was about totals that disagree with their lines. Next to it sits a quieter case: a line whose VAT is exactly half a penny, which the shop rounds up. In the `describe('next door')` block, write tests for it.

The check runs the tests in that block beside the shop's `invoice.js` (they must fail), beside a right fix (they must pass) and beside a version that adds up what the lines show but still rounds decimal numbers (they must fail), on three computers.
nextSteps: Find a line in `invoices.js` whose VAT comes to exactly half a penny.
Work out by hand, in pence, what that line's VAT should be.
Expect the whole invoice for it with `toEqual`, not only the total.
hints: The 5% invoice has a line whose VAT, worked out exactly, ends in a half penny.
10 copies at 2.15 is 2150 pence, and 5% of that is 107.5 pence. The shop rounds a half up.
Expect `invoice([{ title, fee: 2.15, copies: 10 }], 5)` to equal the whole invoice you worked out: its line, its net, its VAT and its total.
